intro: Quito rewards visitors with a UNESCO old town, mountain views and cheap, easy transport. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: Metro runs Quitumbe to El Labrador via Centro Histórico and La Mariscal in about 30 min; fares $0.45 general, $0.22 reduced.
Metro hours: 05:30-23:00 Mon-Fri, 07:00-23:00 Sat, 07:00-22:00 Sun and holidays.
El Trole, Metrobus and Ecovia buses cost about $0.35 per ride; pay at station entrances.
Taxis are yellow with door numbers; day minimum $1, night minimum $2, most city trips under $5.
Easy Taxi and Uber work in Quito; hotels can call a vetted taxi.
Old town is best on foot and car-free on Sundays; bikes allowed on Metro off-peak, first and last cars only.

historic-centre.name: Historic Centre of Quito
historic-centre.price_text: Free to walk · individual churches charge USD 2–5
historic-centre.hours: Streets always open · churches roughly 09:00–17:00, check on the day
historic-centre.tip: Start at Plaza Grande in the morning and walk downhill to La Ronda before the afternoon rain.

middle-of-world.name: Middle of the World City (Ciudad Mitad del Mundo)
middle-of-world.price_text: ≈ USD 5 entry to the monument complex; planetarium and extras cost more
middle-of-world.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–18:00, check on the day
middle-of-world.tip: Bring your passport for a souvenir stamp at the equator line. The nearby Intiñan site has the fun experiments.

la-compania.name: Church of the Society of Jesus (La Compañía)
la-compania.landmark: Church of the Society of Jesus
la-compania.hours: Mon–Sat roughly 09:30–17:30 · Sun afternoon only, check on the day
la-compania.tip: The gold leaf covers almost every surface. No flash photos and keep your voice down.

panecillo.name: Virgin of El Panecillo
panecillo.price_text: ≈ USD 1 to climb the statue; hill access free
panecillo.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00, check on the day
panecillo.tip: Take a taxi up rather than walking. The view over the old town is the real reason to come.

basilica.name: Basilica of the National Vow
basilica.price_text: ≈ USD 3 church · extra to climb the towers
basilica.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00, check on the day
basilica.tip: The tower climb uses steep ladders and narrow walkways. Skip it if you dislike heights.

capilla-hombre.name: Capilla del Hombre
capilla-hombre.tip: Pair it with the artist's house next door. The two tickets are usually sold together.

carondelet.name: Carondelet Palace
carondelet.price_text: Free · guided visits only, book ahead
carondelet.hours: Guided tours on selected days, roughly 09:00–16:00, check on the day
carondelet.tip: Bring photo ID and book a slot in advance. The changing of the guard on the plaza is worth timing.

el-pisque.name: El Pisque Adventure Park
el-pisque.price_text: Per-activity pricing; check on the day
el-pisque.tip: It sits outside the city near the valley towns. Confirm transport and opening before you go.

la-ronda.name: La Ronda
la-ronda.price_text: Free to walk · food and drink extra
la-ronda.hours: Street always open · bars and shops busiest evenings
la-ronda.tip: Come after dark for music and canelazo. Keep valuables close and take a taxi back.

vulqano.name: Vulqano Park
vulqano.price_text: Entry plus per-ride tickets; check on the day
vulqano.hours: Mostly weekends and school holidays, roughly 10:00–18:00
vulqano.tip: Good for families with kids. Check the ride schedule before travelling out.

mercado-central.name: Mercado Central
mercado-central.tip: Go before noon for a cheap set lunch of soup, rice and meat. Try the fruit juices.

teleferico.name: TelefériQo cable car
teleferico.price_text: ≈ USD 9 return; check on the day
teleferico.tip: Go early on a clear morning. Clouds often close the top by afternoon, and it is cold up there.

parque-carolina.name: Parque La Carolina
parque-carolina.tip: A big green space with a botanical garden and running paths. Good for a relaxed afternoon.

la-floresta-walk.name: La Floresta neighbourhood walk
la-floresta-walk.tip: Wander the quiet streets for cafés and street art. Stay on busy streets after dark.

la-mariscal-walk.name: La Mariscal evening walk
la-mariscal-walk.tip: The main dining and nightlife district. Agree taxi fares or use an app, and watch your bag.

city-tour.name: Old town walking tour
city-tour.price_text: ≈ USD 10–25 tip-based or fixed; check on the day
city-tour.tip: A guide helps you read the churches and plazas. Confirm the meeting point and price first.

panecillo-view.name: El Panecillo viewpoint
panecillo-view.tip: Best panorama of the old town and the volcanoes. Take a taxi both ways and go in daylight.

mercado-san-francisco.name: Mercado San Francisco
mercado-san-francisco.tip: Small market near the plaza. Good for a quick local breakfast or fruit.

plaza-grande.name: Plaza Grande (Plaza de la Independencia)
plaza-grande.tip: The heart of the old town, ringed by the palace and cathedral. A good place to start your walk.

cafe-culture.name: Coffee and chocolate tasting
cafe-culture.price_text: ≈ USD 15–30 per tasting; check on the day
cafe-culture.tip: Ecuador grows fine cacao and coffee. A short tasting is a good rainy-afternoon plan.

styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Gold churches, colonial streets and Andean markets.

styles.label: Nature
styles.blurb: Volcano views, cloud forest and the high páramo.

styles.label: Food
styles.blurb: Market lunches, ceviche and strong highland coffee.

stays.why: Walk to the churches, plazas and museums. Quiet at night; car-free on Sundays. Many hostels and small hotels.
Backpacker and nightlife zone with the most restaurants and tour agencies. Metro stop nearby.
Modern, safe and green next to the big park and malls. Good for families and business trips.
Local, bohemian neighbourhood with cafés and food spots. Between the old town and the park.

food: Try locro de papa (potato and cheese soup), hornado (roast pork) and llapingachos (cheese potato patties).
Set lunches (almuerzos) at small restaurants cost about $3–5: soup, main and juice. Great value.
Visit a market: Mercado Central or San Francisco for fruit, juices and cheap local plates.
Ceviche and seafood are good; highland trout is a common dish. Wash it down with canelazo (hot spiced drink).
Coffee is a local pride. Look for small specialty cafés in La Floresta and La Mariscal.
more_time: Add a day for the TelefériQo cable car and a short walk on the Pichincha slopes. Go early; clouds build by midday.
Swap a city afternoon for Mitad del Mundo and the Intiñan site on the equator, about an hour north.
Take a day trip to Cotopaxi National Park for volcano views and páramo walks. Book a tour; altitude is high.
